analyst_view.overall: Early view: Cagliari under Fabio Pisacane ended a four-game losing run with a home win before the international break, while Venezia have picked up results since Davide Nicola replaced the sacked Giovanni Stroppa in mid-October. Nicola built his name on dogged survival fights, so this looks like a tight, careful game between a mid-table side and a bottom-three side. Team news nearer the date will matter, with Cagliari carrying several knocks.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean slightly lower: Nicola's teams usually tighten up first and Venezia are fighting for survival, while Cagliari's attack has been hit by knocks to Nzola and Fadera, who both hoped to be back after the break.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners. Nothing in the news points either way; Cagliari at home should have more of the ball and push wide, while Venezia sit deeper, which fits the site's split.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.0 cards. I lean a little higher because a relegation-threatened Venezia under Nicola tend to make games physical and stop counters, and Cagliari had Obert sent off against Roma recently. The referee is not yet known.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots. I lean lower: a cautious Venezia under Nicola are unlikely to match Cagliari's shot count, and the away side's 14.2 looks generous for a team that will defend deep.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. I lean slightly lower in line with a tight game, with Cagliari's front line short of a fit, in-form striker if Nzola's hamstring is slow to settle.
